 This Mfa Is Filed U/S 173(1) Of Mv Act Against The
Judgment And Award Dated 27.07.2015 Passed In Mvc No.
33/2012 On The File Of The Additional Senior Civil Judge,
Chickballapur, Dismissing The Claim Petition For
Compensation.
 This Appeal, Coming On For Final Hearing, This Day,
Judgment Was Delivered Therein As Under:
Coram: Hon'Ble Mr Justice T.G. Shivashankare Gowda
 Oral Judgment
In this case, the petitioner is challenging the order of dismissal of the claim petition.

2. For the sake of convenience, the rank of the parties shall be referred to as per their status before
the Tribunal.

3.  Brief facts of the case are that on 24.12.2010, while the petitioner was riding the TVS XL motorcycle bearing registration No. KA.40-E-1515, at 6.00 p.m., a tractor bearing No.KA-40-T-4738 hit against the motorcycle, due to which the petitioner has sustained injuries.
After taking treatment at Chandra Mohan Nursing Home, Madanapalli and SNR Hospital at Kolar, the petitioner has approached the Tribunal for grant of compensation.

The claim was opposed by the respondents, and the Tribunal, after recording the evidence and hearing both NC: 2024:KHC:37634 the parties,
dismissed the claim petition.
Aggrieved by the same, the petitioner is before this Court.

4. Heard the arguments of Smt. Suguna R. Re ddy, learned counsel for the petitioner and Sri.
A.M.Venkatesh, learned counsel for respondent No.2/Insurance Company.

Sri. T.R.Ramesh,
learned counsel for respondent No.1 remained absent.
5. It is contended by the learned counsel for the petitioner that the petitioner was from Andrapradesh.
Soon after the accident, he went to his place at Madanapalli and took treatment and thereafter, he took treatment at SNR Hospital, Kolar and medical records have been placed before the Tribunal.
Since the petitioner was under hospitalization, he did not file the complaint with the police.

For this reason, a complaint was filed on 15.01.2011 and there is a delay of 22 days in the filing the complaint and reason for the delay is explained as hospitalization on account of the injuries sustained in the road accident.

The Police have registered the case against the driver of the tractor and he has been charge NC: 2024:KHC:37634 sheeted for the actionable negligence and the driver has pleaded guilty before the learned Magistrate.

5.1. It is further contended that, before the Tribunal, the owner of the tractor has admitted the occurrence of the accident, policy of insurance is in force, the driver was having a valid driving license at the time of the accident.

But the Tribunal has erroneously dismissed the claim only on the ground that there is a delay in filing the complaint, no proper explanation is offered and she sought Sri. Vemana Naik M vs Sri. K.B. Krishna Reddy on 12 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/111866549/
2 for assessment of the compensation and direction to the respondents to pay the compensation.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
6. Per contra, learned counsel for the Insurance Company has contended that after the accident on 24.12.2010, the petitioner has taken treatment at Chandra Mohan Nursing Home at Madanapalli,
where the history of the accident is furnished and same is produced at Ex.R1.
It is recited in the said document that the petitioner has sustained injuries due to falling from the bike.

Neither in the records of Chandra Mohan Nursing Home nor in the records of SNR Hospital, there is any mention that the petitioner has been involved in an accident hit NC: 2024:KHC:37634 by the tractor in question.

Only after 22 days, the tractor was first time born in the police station, charge sheet was formally filed, the driver of the tractor was got pleaded guilty and the owner of the tractor admitted the accident before the Tribunal.
All these being mechanically done for the sake of compensation and fraud is played against the Insurance Company.
The Tribunal is right in dismissing the claim petition and he supported the impugned judgment.
7. I have given my anxious consideration to the arguments advanced by learned counsel for both parties and perused the material on record.
8. The prosecution papers go to explain that there was an accident occured on 24.12.2010 involving a Tractor and TVS Motorcycle.
The petitioner was the rider of the TVS motorcycle along with one Gouse Moliddun as a pillion rider.
It is alleged in the compliant that the tractor had hit against the motorcycle.
From the place of accident, the petitioner gone to Madanapalli and informed Chandra Mohan Nursing Home that he has sustained fracture of right tibia due to falling down from the bike.
In the said history there is no whisper that the NC: 2024:KHC:37634 tractor had hit against the motorcycle.
The complaint was filed on 15.1.2011 incorporating the tractor.
If the petitioner was very well aware that the tractor caused the accident, he ought to have mentioned that the tractor hit against his bike.
Mere mentioning in the hospital that there was an RTI is not sufficient.
How the petitioner came to know about the registration number of the tractor to incorporate the same in the complaint is not explained.

After 22 days, all of a sudden, the tractor was found and the manner in which the owner of the tractor admitted the accident and his driver appeared before the learned Magistrate on the first date of hearing and pleading guilty clearly goes to show the hand in glove between the petitioner and the owner of the tractor.
Hence, it is the clear case of fraud.

In the light of the judgment of the Division Bench of this Court in the case of Veerappa and Another Vs.
Siddappa and Another reported in ILR 2009 KAR 3562 rather dismissing the claim, it is the fit case to assess the compensation and direct the owner of the tractor to pay the compensation.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 9. As regards the quantum of compensation, the petitioner suffered fracture of right tibia and was under NC: 2024:KHC:37634 hospitalization for 16 days.
He has underwent surgery twice and spent towards treatment and suffered an loss of amenities and discomfort, the medical bills stand at Rs.43,359/-.

P.W.2 Dr. K.R.Ananthu, Orthopaedic surgeon,
made the assessment of disability to an extent of 15% to the whole body.
Having regard to the fracture of the right tibia, it is proper to assess the personal disability at 10%.
Notional Income of the petitioner has to be taken at Rs.5,500/-.

The multiplier Sri. Vemana Naik M vs Sri. K.B. Krishna Reddy on 12 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/111866549/
3 applicable to his age is '17'.

entities.text: Vemana Naik M vs Sri. K.B. Krishna Reddy
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Then loss of future income is 5,500x12x17x10% =
1,12,200/- and the same is awarded towards loss of future earnings.

10. Towards 'Pain and Suffering', the petitioner has to be compensated awarded with Rs.30,000/-,
'Medical Expenses' at Rs.43,359/-, towards 'Loss of Amenities and Discomfort' is Rs.25,000/-.
'Food, Nourishment and Conveyance' is Rs.15,000/-, 'Loss of Income' during the laid up period of five months is Rs.27,500/-.
Total compensation comes to Rs.2,53,059/- and it is the just compensation that the petitioner is entitled to in the facts and circumstances of the case.

In view of the above discussions, the appeal merits consideration, in the result, the following:
JUDGMENT i) The appeal is allowed in part.
ii) The impugned judgment and award is set aside.
iii) The petitioner would be entitled to compensation of Rs.2,53,059/- with interest at 6% per annum from the date of the petition till the date of deposit.
iv) The owner of the tractor i.e., respondent No.1 is directed to pay the compensation with interest and shall deposit the same within eight weeks from today.
v) The order of dismissal of the claim against the Insurance Company stands confirmed.

SD/-
